passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following is management's discussion and analysis of certain significant factors which have affected our financial position and operating results during the periods included in the accompanying consolidated financial statements and should be read in conjunction with those consolidated financial statements. This section of the Form 10-K generally discusses 2025 and 2024 items and year-to-year comparisons between the years. Discussions of 2023 comparisons can be found in our 2024 Annual Report filed with the SEC. Business and Operational Overview Fastenal is a global leader in the wholesale distribution of industrial and construction supplies. We distribute these supplies through a network of approximately 1,600 branch locations. Our largest end market is manufacturing. Sales to these customers include products for both direct materials, where our products are consumed in the final products of our customers, and indirect materials, where our products are consumed to support the facilities and ongoing operations of our customers. We also service general and commercial contractors in non-residential end markets as well as farmers, truckers, railroads, oil exploration companies, oil production and refinement companies, mining companies, federal, state, and local government entities, schools, warehouse and storage, data centers, and certain retail trades. Geographically, our selling locations and customers are primarily located in North America, though we continue to grow our non-North American presence as well. It is helpful to appreciate several aspects of our marketplace: First, it is big and fragmented. We estimate the North American marketplace for industrial supplies is in excess of $140 billion per year (and we have expanded beyond North America) and no company has a significant portion of this market. Second, many of the products we sell are individually inexpensive, but the cost and time to manage, procure, and transport these products can be quite meaningful. Third, many customers prefer to reduce their number of indirect and direct suppliers to simplify their business, while also utilizing various technologies and models (including our local branches when they need something quickly or unexpectedly) to improve availability and reduce waste. Lastly, we believe the markets are efficient. In our view, this means that companies who grow market share are those that develop differentiated capabilities that provide the greatest value to the customer. Our approach to addressing these aspects of our marketplace is captured in our motto Growth Through Customer Service ® and our tagline Where Industry Meets Innovation ™ . The concept of growth is simple: find more customers every day that value the services we provide and increase our activity with them. However, execution is hard work. First, we recruit service-minded individuals to support customers and empower them to operate in a decentralized fashion to maximize their flexibility to solve customer problems. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: In addition to the other information in this Form 10-K, the following factors should be considered in evaluating our business. Our operating results depend upon many factors and are subject to various risks and uncertainties. The material risks and uncertainties known to us which may cause our operating results to vary from anticipated results or which may negatively affect our operating results and profitability are as follows: Company-Specific Risks Operational Risks Products that we sell may expose us to potential material liability for property damage, environmental damage, personal injury, or death linked to the use of those products by our customers. Some of our customers operate in challenging industries in which there is a material risk of catastrophic events. We are actively seeking to expand our sales to certain categories of customers, some of whose businesses may entail heightened levels of such risk. If any of these events are linked to the use of any of our products by our customers, claims could be brought against us by those customers, by governmental authorities, and by third parties who are injured or damaged as a result of such events. In addition, our reputation could be adversely affected by negative publicity surrounding such events regardless of whether or not claims against us are successful. While we maintain insurance coverage to mitigate a portion of this risk and may have recourse against our suppliers for losses arising out of defects in products procured from them, we could experience significant losses as a result of claims made against us to the extent adequate insurance is not in place, the products are manufactured by us or legal recourse against our suppliers is otherwise not available, or our insurers or suppliers are unwilling or unable to satisfy their obligations to us. Interruptions in the proper functioning of information systems or the inability to maintain or upgrade our information systems, or convert to alternate systems in a timely and efficient manner, could disrupt operations, cause unanticipated increases in costs and/or decreases in sales, and result in less efficient operations. The proper functioning of our information systems is critical to many aspects of our business and we could be adversely affected if we experience a disruption or data loss relating to our information systems and are unable to recover in a timely manner. Our information systems are protected with robust backup systems and processes, including physical and software safeguards and remote processing capabilities. Still, information systems are vulnerable to natural disasters, power losses, unauthorized access, cybersecurity incidents, telecommunication failures, and other problems. In addition, certain software used by us is licensed from, and certain services related to our information systems are provided by, third parties who could choose to discontinue their products or services or their relationship with us. It is also possible that we are unable to improve, upgrade, maintain, and expand our information systems. credit_strengths.text: Fastenal's operating cash flow comfortably covers capital expenditure, leaving substantial free cash flow that exceeds reported debt by a wide margin. This internally generated liquidity, combined with a large cash balance, produces a net cash position and minimal leverage, positioning the issuer far stronger than the sector median on both cash-flow coverage and balance-sheet gearing.

The debt structure is modest and well laddered, with senior unsecured notes maturing across several years and an undrawn committed revolver providing backup liquidity. Interest coverage is exceptionally high, and the current ratio signals ample short-term liquidity. These features reduce refinancing risk and support a minimal indicative financial risk profile.

key_risks.text: The debt note discloses that the master note agreement's aggregate borrowing capacity is largely uncommitted, meaning institutional investors are not obligated to purchase notes. If the issuer needed to draw on this facility, funding could be unavailable, forcing reliance on the revolver or market issuance. This is a structural refinancing vulnerability despite current ample liquidity.

Risk factors highlight potential product liability and information-system disruptions. Product liability claims could arise from customer use of distributed supplies, and insurance may not fully cover losses. Information-system failures or cyber incidents could disrupt order processing, inventory management, and receivables collection, potentially impairing operating cash flow and liquidity generation.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is extraordinarily high, with operating income dwarfing interest expense. Free cash flow to debt also stands at a multiple well above sector norms. This capacity is supported by consistent operating cash flow and low capital intensity. Even if cash flow declined, the issuer could service debt from cash on hand without external refinancing.

The maturity profile is manageable, with only a small current portion of debt due and the revolver undrawn. However, the uncommitted master note capacity means future refinancing depends on investor appetite. Our forward view is that debt service remains comfortably covered, but we monitor the uncommitted facility as a contingent liquidity constraint.

overall_credit_view.text: Fastenal exhibits a minimal indicative financial risk profile, with net cash, negligible leverage, and robust cash generation. Leverage sits far below the sector median, and profitability margins exceed sector norms. The business benefits from a fragmented industrial distribution market and a high-touch service model, supporting revenue growth and operating cash flow resilience.

Our forward-looking judgement is that credit quality remains strong, underpinned by consistent free cash flow and a conservative debt structure. Shareholder distributions absorb most free cash flow, but the net cash position provides a buffer. The primary watch items are the uncommitted master note facility and operational risks from product liability and information systems, which are manageable at current scale.

credit_strengths.text: Fastenal的營運現金流足以輕鬆覆蓋資本開支，留下大量自由現金流，遠超呈報債務。此內部產生的流動性，加上龐大的現金結餘，形成淨現金狀況及極低槓桿，令發行人在現金流覆蓋及資產負債表槓桿方面均遠強於行業中位數。
債務結構適度且到期日分佈良好，高級無抵押票據於數年間陸續到期，而未動用的承諾循環信貸提供備用流動性。利息覆蓋率極高，流動比率亦顯示短期流動性充裕。此等特徵降低再融資風險，並支持極低的指示性財務風險狀況。

key_risks.text: 債務票據披露，主票據協議的總借款能力大部分為非承諾性，意味著機構投資者並無義務購買票據。若發行人需要動用此融資，資金可能無法獲得，迫使依賴循環信貸或市場發行。儘管目前流動性充裕，此乃結構性再融資弱點。
風險因素強調潛在的產品責任及資訊系統中斷。產品責任索賠可能因客戶使用所分銷的用品而產生，而保險未必能完全覆蓋損失。資訊系統故障或網絡事件可能中斷訂單處理、庫存管理及應收賬款回收，可能損害營運現金流及流動性產生。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率極高，營運收入遠超利息開支。自由現金流對債務的倍數亦遠高於行業常態。此能力由穩定的營運現金流及低資本密集度支持。即使現金流下降，發行人亦可利用手頭現金償還債務，無需外部再融資。
到期結構可控，僅有少量流動部分債務到期，而循環信貸未動用。然而，非承諾性主票據能力意味著未來再融資取決於投資者意欲。我們的前瞻觀點是債務償付仍獲穩健覆蓋，但我們將非承諾性融資視為或然流動性限制並加以監察。

overall_credit_view.text: Fastenal展現極低的指示性財務風險狀況，擁有淨現金、微不足道的槓桿及強勁的現金產生能力。槓桿遠低於行業中位數，而盈利能力利潤率則高於行業常態。該業務受益於分散的工業分銷市場及高接觸服務模式，支持收入增長及營運現金流韌性。
我們的前瞻性判斷是信貸質素保持強勁，由穩定的自由現金流及保守的債務結構支撐。股東分派吸收大部分自由現金流，但淨現金狀況提供緩衝。主要觀察事項為非承諾性主票據融資及來自產品責任與資訊系統的營運風險，此等在目前規模下屬可控。
